feat(loom-myhi.2): claim-provenance return contract in dispatched-agent rules

Adds a "## Claim provenance in worker returns (loom-myhi)" section to
.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md as a sibling to the loom-z3m.16
sampling-transparency clause, carrying design decisions D2 + D5 + D6.

D2 — the evidence slot. Every load-bearing claim carries either a
citation (command + result, or file:line) or the literal marker
INFERRED. The slot is a POINTER, not a rationale: it says where to
look, not why to believe, so no justifying prose goes in it.

Both surface forms are documented, because a bracket-only description
understates the shipped contract and would skip every triple report:
  - bracket form, prose reports: a trailing bracketed token ends the
    claim line.
  - field form, triple reports (agents/kg-relationship-extractor.md:35):
    a LINE-LEADING `evidence:` field, matched anchored (^\s*evidence:),
    parallel to loom's Files: / RED: / AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: convention.

Both arrow glyphs are documented — ASCII ` -> ` and Unicode ` → `
(U+2192). Measured on main, the shipped agent defs use Unicode
exclusively (grep -c ' -> ' → 0/0/0; ' → ' → 1/2/9), so pinning one
glyph would miss every real command citation in the wild.

F1 is stated as "zero slots of either form", never "zero brackets" — a
bracket-free triple report is fully evidenced and passes.

D5 — refutation is two-field: `verdict` (was it true, and why) and
`residue` (was it pointing at anything, or the literal `none`). Residue
may be `none` but may not be absent: a refuted claim can still be
load-bearing, and a binary accept/reject discards that.

D6 — file before acting: central may not make a change on the basis of
an INFERRED claim without filing it first; the filed bead is where the
verdict + residue land. Un-acted-on claims just stay in the worklist.

The new test section is DOCUMENTATION-PRESENCE ONLY and says so in an
inline comment naming scripts/loom-claim-provenance (loom-myhi.1) as the

green suite and concludes the contract is enforced, which is the exact

Done. `loom-myhi.2` implemented, committed on `frank/…` branch, not pushed, not merged, bead left open per brief.

## What I added and where

**`.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md:587`** — new section `## Claim provenance in worker returns (loom-myhi)`, +113 lines, placed immediately after `## Worker-report sampling transparency (loom-z3m.16)` (ended at :585) and before `## Central-side pre-dispatch repo check`. [`grep -n '^## Claim provenance in worker returns' .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md` → `587`]

**`lib/tests/dispatched-agents-rule.test.sh:378`** — new section 12, +90 lines, 21 assertions. [`grep -n 'Claim-provenance return contract (loom-myhi.2' lib/tests/dispatched-agents-rule.test.sh` → `378`]

Voice matched to the sampling section: `**Risk (…)**` → `**Convention — …**` → `**Mechanical fix.**` bold lead-ins, 72-col wrap, no numbered battery steps. [`.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md:564-585`]

## The two forms and the glyph rule, verbatim

Two forms:

> *Bracket form*, in prose reports (dispatched workers, `drawer-author`, `bug-family-researcher`, `project-onboarder`). A trailing bracketed token ends the claim line:

> *Field form*, in structured triple reports (`agents/kg-relationship-extractor.md:35`). Triples are not sentences and already carry a `*Why*` line, so bracketing would collapse the slot into the rationale — exactly what D2 splits apart. The slot is instead a **line-leading `evidence:` field**, matched anchored (`^\s*evidence:`), parallel to loom's `Files:` / `RED:` / `AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE:` convention — so a mid-prose mention of the word is not a slot

Glyph rule:

> **Both arrow glyphs.** In either form, a payload containing an arrow is a **command citation**: the command is the text before the arrow, the result after. The separator may be ASCII ` -> ` **or** Unicode ` → ` (U+2192), and both are accepted. This is not cosmetic — measured on the shipped agent definitions, the Unicode arrow is used *exclusively* (`grep -c ' -> ' agents/drawer-author.md agents/bug-family-researcher.md agents/kg-relationship-extractor.md` → `0/0/0`; the same count for ` → ` → `1/2/9`), while ASCII is what gets typed in prose. Pinning one glyph would miss every real command citation in the wild.

F1:

> **F1 is "zero slots of either form" — never "zero brackets".** A bracket-free triple report whose triples each carry an `evidence:` line is fully evidenced and PASSES. Counting brackets would fail an entire agent's output for using the form that agent is specified to use.

I re-measured the glyph counts rather than trusting the brief. [`grep -c ' -> ' …` → `bug-family-researcher:0, kg-relationship-extractor:0, drawer-author:0`; `grep -c ' → '` → `2, 9, 1` respectively]

## The document-presence caveat comment — present

`lib/tests/dispatched-agents-rule.test.sh:381`, a 20-line block opening:

> `# *** THESE ARE DOCUMENTATION-PRESENCE ASSERTIONS, NOT THE GATE. ***`

It states the assertions prove only that the rule text is written down and that no assertion reads a returned report; names exploration F9 and the existing `Processed: X of Y` assertion (section 9) as the same fake-gate shape in this very file; names `scripts/loom-claim-provenance` (loom-myhi.1) as the real behavioural gate with its F1/F2 conditions; declares `lib/tests/loom-claim-provenance.test.sh` authoritative — **"if these doc patterns and that test ever disagree about the contract, THAT TEST WINS"**; and closes `# Do not read a green run of this section as "the contract is enforced".` The `echo` banner also carries it inline: `==> Claim-provenance return contract (DOC PRESENCE — gate is scripts/loom-claim-provenance)`.

## Judgment calls

- **[INFERRED] The bead notes and the design drawer disagree about the drawer's own arrow glyph, and it does not matter.** The notes say "The design doc's D2 example uses ASCII", and `scripts/loom-claim-provenance:45-46` repeats that claim. The drawer's D2 example is actually Unicode: `[go test -run TestScan -count=1 → 4/4]`. [drawer `drawer_loom_decisions_1a296178707cdc55c872b467`, D2 section] Since the test is authoritative and it requires **both** glyphs regardless, I sidestepped it — my prose attributes the exclusive-Unicode measurement to the agent defs (which I verified myself) and says only that "ASCII is what gets typed in prose", asserting nothing about the design doc. Worth a follow-up only if someone wants the reader's header comment corrected; it has zero behavioural effect.
- **[INFERRED] Plain ``` fences rather than ```bash for the two report excerpts.** The existing awk gate (test section 5) only scans ```bash blocks, and only inside the battery section, so ```bash would not have tripped it — but plain fences are also semantically correct here and remove the coupling entirely.
- **[INFERRED] No `CLAUDE.md` bullet added.** The convention bullets there mirror rule-file sections, so one arguably belongs — but `CLAUDE.md` is outside this bead's `Files:`, and loom-myhi.5 (docs) / loom-myhi.6 (owned template) cover downstream propagation.
